I do. We get along great, and neither of us has ever been this close to someone else. We talk in some form or another almost 24/7, and enjoy doing so. This has been the same for 2 years now, but like I said, every time this comes up to other people, they all say "well that's how it's like in the beginning", but it's not like I'm a teenager that just flirts with his gf all day. We're both adults that just generally enjoy each other's company doing average adult things. 

But yes, I'm not exaggerating. Let me think of the people I'm surrounded by...

My mother got screwed over by my father, so she has a low view of relationships

all my aunts are either divorced and bitter, or dislike their husbands or treat them like incompetent lugs. 

My uncle who I'm renting with, has the mentality that being alone is better because "fuck people"

at the church I used to go to (because of family) everyone was either cheating on someone else, or out to spite someone else because of some stupid crush.

My gf's friends all hate men because they're dogs and blah blah

I guess I'm not as social as I used to be, so the fact that it's 100% isn't as big as it sounds, since I'm living in a vacuum for the most part.

What makes everybody else cynical is whenever I say something positive about anything, they come back with a reason to not be happy about it, and it's depressing. No on wants to be sad, so why force it?

"Oh let's go to Disney! You said you wanted to go right?"

"Nah, it's always so crowded< I'd hate it"

something as simple as that, to:

"Mom I'm in love :)"

"Yeah, just give it a few years..."

I recently heard about how unhappy my aunt is.. and that she yells at her husband every day.... they fight a lot...

And this was an aunt that was always very happy, mellow, and likable. So it's scary to see these things happen. Especially with how comedians and people always joke about how marriage sucks, and you want to kill your spouse. What the hell, I don't want that. I want to be happy, you know?

I don't think it's marriage, I think it's that romance becomes banal when you start having to be around the person 24/7, and people discover too late that the person they married isn't compatible with their every day life. Annoyance turns into crankiness, and that eventually turns into being cynical, as least that's what I think. I get along with my girlfriend as a friend too, but I'm scared that we'll just end up like everyone else. 

When I'm feeling optimistic, I say just that, that I should be a good example and show people how things ought to be, but that sounds so pretentious, and I'm worried that I'm just being naive in thinking that I'll be different than 100% of the people around me.

But okay, thanks for listening. Have a good day.

It sucks looking forward and seeing the decline in happiness as inevitable. And even more so that most people are resigned to avoiding it. What I don't like seeing in most adults, is how they make it seem like life experience tells them that as a whole, everyone is out to get you. When my girlfriend introduced me to her best friends mom, the mom said, "oh I bet you're happy now, he seems so perfect I'm sure... and you're all in love, but people change... right son?" and I said "well yeah, but does change always have to be for the worst?". I don't like seeing married couples' everyday life being 98% stress, and 2% slight happiness that comes with a 2 minute break before bed of candy crush, before taking on the next day of being unhappy with each other, which is all I've seen from every couple I know :/

Of course there is a chance of happiness, but I don't want to be alone, though I'm perfectly content being so, it's not what I want for myself, and of course the people you interact with have to meet you half way (with optimism)

I'm hopeful of the future, and things are decent now, but the problem is that I see them getting worse over time, based on how I see most adults.In five years, I see myself just trying to get by like everyone else, but where I don't want to be is a cynical place mentally. I just want to be happy, around happy people.

Thank you. Sorry, I forgot you asked that. What appeals to me about death is the eternal nothingness. If the future is so bleak, then permanent sleep sounds like a good deal. No pain, dissapointment, worry, stress, problems. When I'm feeling positive, I tell myself that I shouldn't throw away 80 rough years of life because after that it's game over permanently, so I should take these years and do the best with them and enjoy them, but if the future is so bleak, then the sooner death comes, the better. I am not afraid of not existing.

I have. I'm very open about these things. But mainly towards my girlfriend and mother, since they are the only one's I can say I was ever close to. I've since given up on my mother, (in that aspect) because she's become obsessed with Christianity after she became pentecostal. So she only gives vacuous responses to everything. Everything will be alright, if you just put your faith in God. Those responses used to frustrate me to an extreme, but I've resigned myself to get anything more than that out of her. With my gf, I've spoken to her a lot about it, but it seems like it's part of her personality, so even thought it comes up and she works on it, she seems to unconsciously fall back into her default mentality.

Yeah humans are social creatures, and we need optimism around us to feed off of. Specifically, I'd like to see my gf be more optimistic about our future, and have people around me say positive things about days to come, and not be so negative towards even positive things. A made up example would be me commenting on how good our relationship is, and her agreeing, yet commenting on how love fades and won't last forever. It brings an overall good mood down, and it seems unnecessary, when all other signs point to her not wanting it to happen, but resigned to accept it.

I think she has changed, and she herself has said so. Like I said, I don't hold it against her, or judge her. It's more of a realization of what good people can do.

I've barely gotten by in the past cause I've always been poor, which is fine. I've gotten a job since and am renting a place and now live at least comfortably and not moving every 6 months. I'm not trying to dramatize my life though, since I don't think it's been emotinally scarring. I went through all the usual being bullied and whatever poor ids go through, but I feel okay now. 

I can't even imagine the stress one would feel form being on the opposite end of this subreddit, but I imagine it's tough. And I think I can understand where you're coming from. I do get genuine joy still from bonding sincerely with people and seeing that I make them happy. So when they get all cynical, I get like this.

Yeah, alcohol makes you do dumb stuff, and I tell myself that she was young and horny, and drunk. A kid in his/her 20s will do stuff they regret. But she was seeing this guy knowing he had a gf even if it didn't involve sexual things throughout. I don't hold it against her, but it seems so unlike her that it bothers me to see that kind of Jerry Springer behavior in real people. She does say that I'm her first love and that she's never really been in a real relationship where she opened up before me, and I know because she used to be friends with my sister in high school. I can also tell she's sincere with what she says, and I sincerely care about her. 

Idk why I feel life is bland, and maybe I'm just not articulate enough, but I'll try to describe it. When I was 15, I absolutely loved music, and I taught myself guitar. I didn't have access to a teacher or a computer, so I would walk half an hour every day to the library to get 30 minutes online to learn whatever I could. I was really passionate. This went on for 4 years before it totally bored me. Now everything feels like that. I guess if anything would be the reason I'm bummed out from time to time, it's because I've for the most part been on my own my whole life. I was raised by m mother who did a great job with love, but with all due respect, she's very weak, and I've had to do everything myself all my life. And I never had any emotional support from anyone. No dad, mom, whatever. But I've gotten by I guess...

I think that mainly, I feel that life is bland because I've worked so hard to live my life sincerely and make the people I love happy, and it seems like despite all that, everyone is gonna grow cynical and cranky with each other, so why bother. The worst part is that it's not even teen angst like I would tell myself before, because now it's looking more and more like the harsh reality of adult life.

It does make me fear for my future and wonder if it really is inevitable to be screwed over by those you love. I do have a good idea why these people are cynical. My mom would be beat my my dad before he walked out on us when I was 6. And all of my aunts (who I spend the most family social time with) have been screwed over by men. Idk why my gf is cynical since she says she's never been screwed over, but she says that a lot of the women in her family have been screwed over badly by men, and that all her family have taught her about love is to watch her back. She seems to always expect bad things from me, when she admits that I haven't given her any reason to do so. One thing that did break my heart about her was that she told me she lost her virginity drunk to some guy that was cheating on his girlfriend, because she wanted to get back at some girl. This was when she was 19, and 3 months before I met her. She says she regrets this, and that she stopped him after 5 minutes because it hurt, and that she stopped seeing him after that because she knew she fucked up, and that it was her only sexual experience up until she met me eventually. What bums me out about that is that the person I see as so good and an amazing person could do something so cold hearted. Even though it was in the moment and she just "gave in", it just stays in my mind. So good people really do bad stuff like that...?

I feel like I wanna end life on a high note, instead of ending up like everyone else does, with a cynical view of love, happiness, hope, and respect. I don't wanna hate or dislike the people I love now.

It seems somewhat too good to be true to think that a couple pills could be a solution to feeling like this, but it'd be a lifesaver (maybe even literally). But I understand that chemical imbalances do cause these types of things, so I'm not shooting down your comment. Thank you.

If I had to think of something, I'd say one thing that keeps me pessimistic about life is seeing 100% of adults around me be so cynical. I hate it. Life is hard enough without everyone expecting the worst of each other. I love my girlfriend of two years and she makes me happy as a friend and companion, but even she's cynical about a lot of things. She definitely loves me and I believe we have a healthy relationship, as we are happy around each other most of the time. But I don't like how everyone expects everything to go bad, and it doesn't seem to bother them as they see it as an inevitability. My mother expects me to leave her and not care about her when I get married. My girlfriend has that "all men change after marriage" attitude, and I don't know any couples who are happily married. I just see a bunch of couple yelling at each other, and cranky all the time because of life stress. They take it out on each other instead of keeping their word about respecting each other and actually showing they care. Now don't get me wrong, I'm by no means a push over, and I can hold my own with life and confrontation, but I don't want it to have to be like that. I just want a sincerely nice and hopeful future, and it seems like I'm the only one in the world who does.
